conversation.content:
Hello! I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging that being a new mother can be a truly overwhelming and life-changing experience. It's completely normal to feel a mix of emotions during this time, and I'm here to support you every step of the way.

As part of our conversation today, I'd like to use the EPDS to help us better understand how you're feeling and to identify any potential areas of support that might be helpful to you. The EPDS is a tool that screens for depressive and anxiety symptoms, and it can give us valuable insights into your emotional well-being during the postpartum period.

Please know that everything we discuss today is completely confidential and a safe space for you to express yourself freely. I'm here to listen, support, and provide guidance, not to judge. My goal is to help you feel comfortable and empowered to share your thoughts and feelings with me.

The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help us get a better sense of how you've been feeling over the past week. We'll take it one question at a time, and I'll do my best to make this conversation feel as natural and comfortable as possible. 

To get us started, I'd like to ask: Over the past 7 days, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

Honestly, not as much as I used to. I mean, I still find some things funny, like when my baby does something adorable, but it's just not the same as before. I feel like I've been so tired and preoccupied with worrying about the baby's safety and everything else that I just don't seem to enjoy things as much. Like, my husband will try to make me laugh, and I'll smile, but it's just not as effortless as it used to be. And some days, I just feel really sad and discouraged, and it's hard to see the funny side of anything. But, I don't know, maybe that's just me being a new mom and everything is just overwhelming? (sighs) Sorry, I don't know if that makes sense...
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

I wish I could say that's been me, but like I said, it's just been really hard to find the humor in things lately. I feel like I'm just going through the motions most days, trying to take care of the baby and keep everything together, but it's exhausting. And when I'm not feeling anxious or worried, I just feel really sad and overwhelmed. I do get some pleasure from a few things, like watching my baby sleep or seeing her little smile, but it's just not the same as before. Everything feels so different now, and it's hard to explain. Sometimes I feel like I'm just pretending to be a good mom, but inside, I'm just struggling to keep up. (pauses, looking down) Sorry, it's just really hard to talk about this...
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

(sighs) To be honest, not really. I mean, I used to love doing things like going out with friends, trying new restaurants, or just watching a movie with my husband. But now, it all just feels so overwhelming. Even thinking about leaving the house with the baby feels like a huge task. I just don't have the energy for it, and to be honest, I've been having a lot of trouble sleeping, which doesn't help. Some nights, I'll wake up and just lie there, thinking about all the things that could go wrong with the baby, and it's hard to calm myself down. And when I do manage to fall asleep, I usually wake up feeling exhausted. I've been trying to take care of the baby, but it's just been really hard to enjoy things like I used to. I've been feeling really guilty about it too, like I'm not being a good enough mom because I'm not enjoying every moment of this. But the truth is, most days I just feel really sad and discouraged, and I don't know how to get out of this rut. (looks down, fidgeting with hands) Sometimes I feel like I'm just going through the motions, you know? And it's hard to explain, but even when I do find some joy in things, it's just not the same as before. I've had some fleeting thoughts of self-harm, but they're not constant, and I don't have any plans or intent to act on them. It's just...I don't know, it feels like everything is just too much for me right now.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

(nods, looking down) Yeah, that sounds like me. I feel like I'm always blaming myself for something. If the baby is crying, I think it's because I'm not doing something right. If she's not sleeping well, I think it's because I didn't establish a good routine. If she's not eating enough, I think it's because I'm not producing enough milk. It's just this constant feeling of "I'm not doing enough" or "I'm not doing it right". And it's not just with the baby, it's with everything. I feel like I'm just making mistake after mistake, and it's all my fault. Sometimes I catch myself thinking "What kind of mother am I?" or "Why can't I just get this right?" It's like I'm my own worst critic. (pauses, taking a deep breath) And it's exhausting, you know? It's like I'm always walking around with this weight of guilt and self-doubt. I just wish I could be kinder to myself, but it's hard when I feel like everything is riding on my shoulders. (looks up, eyes welling up with tears) Sorry, it's just really hard to talk about this...
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

(nods, tears streaming down her face) Oh, yeah... that's me all the time. I mean, I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll just start worrying about something. Like, what if she stops breathing? What if I'm not producing enough milk? What if someone breaks into the house and hurts us? It's just this constant stream of worst-case scenarios playing in my head, and it's hard to shut it off. Sometimes I'll be awake at 3am, just lying there, thinking about all the things that could go wrong, and I'll feel my heart racing and my mind spinning. It's like I'm always on high alert, waiting for something to go wrong. And it's not just the big things, it's the little things too. Like, what if I forget to buckle her car seat? What if I give her too much medicine? It's just this never-ending cycle of worry and fear, and it's exhausting. (cries) I just wish I could feel calm and peaceful, you know? Like, I wish I could just enjoy this time with my baby without all this anxiety weighing me down. (sniffles) Sorry, it's just really hard to deal with...
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

(nods, still sniffling) Yeah, that's happened to me too. I'll be doing something normal, like taking a shower or making breakfast, and suddenly I'll just feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, my breath will get caught in my throat, and I'll feel like I'm going to pass out. It's like my body is reacting to some kind of threat, but there's no threat there. It's just... nothing. And it's so scary, because I don't know what's happening or how to make it stop. Sometimes I'll be holding the baby, and I'll just feel this overwhelming sense of fear, like something is going to happen to her, or to me, or to us. And it's not just when I'm alone, it's even when my husband is there, and he's trying to calm me down, and I just can't shake this feeling of panic. (shakes her head) It's like my mind is playing tricks on me, and I don't know how to stop it. (pauses, taking a deep breath) And the worst part is, sometimes I'll have these thoughts, like... really dark thoughts. About hurting myself, or... (pauses, looking down) I don't know, it's just really scary, and I don't know how to deal with it. (starts to cry again) Sorry...
Things have been getting on top of me

(nods, crying) Oh, yeah... that's exactly how I feel. Like, everything is just piling up on me, and I don't know how to keep up. Taking care of the baby, and the house, and my relationship with my husband... it's all just so much. And I feel like I'm failing at everything. I'm not a good enough mom, I'm not a good enough wife, I'm not a good enough person... (sobs) It's just this constant feeling of overwhelm, like I'm drowning in responsibilities and emotions. And I don't know how to keep my head above water. Sometimes I feel like I'm just pretending to be a functioning adult, but really I'm just barely holding it together. (shakes her head) And the worst part is, I feel like I'm all alone in this. Like, my husband tries to help, but he doesn't understand what I'm going through. And my friends and family, they all seem to be doing so much better than me... (cries) It's just really hard to feel like I'm the only one who's struggling. (pauses, taking a deep breath) I just wish someone could take some of the weight off my shoulders, you know? Like, just give me a break, and let me catch my breath... (sobs) Sorry, I'm just really struggling right now...
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

(nods, tears streaming down her face) Yes, that's me. I've been having so much trouble sleeping lately. I'll lie awake at night, thinking about all the things that are worrying me, and I just can't seem to calm my mind down. I'll think about the baby, and whether she's okay, and whether I'm doing everything right... and it just spirals out of control. Sometimes I'll wake up in the middle of the night, and I'll just lie there, feeling anxious and overwhelmed. And even when I do fall asleep, I don't feel rested. I feel like I'm just going through the motions, you know? Like, I'm not really sleeping, I'm just existing. (sighs) And it's hard, because I know I need sleep to be a good mom, but it's just not happening. I've been feeling so unhappy and overwhelmed, and it's like my body is just reflecting that. I'll be awake for hours, just lying there, feeling miserable... (cries) It's just really hard to deal with. Sometimes I'll get up, and I'll just walk around the house, trying to calm myself down, but it's hard to shake the feeling of sadness and worry. (pauses, taking a deep breath) I just wish I could sleep, you know? Like, really sleep, without all these thoughts and worries racing through my mind. (sobs) Sorry, it's just really hard right now...
I have felt sad or miserable

(nods, tears streaming down her face) Yes, that's me. I've been feeling so sad and miserable lately. It's like this constant cloud of sadness is following me everywhere I go. I'll be doing something with the baby, and I'll just start crying, because it's all just feeling so overwhelming. I feel like I'm losing myself in all of this, like I'm just a mom now, and not a person anymore. (sobs) I miss the person I used to be, the person who could laugh and have fun and not worry about everything all the time. I feel like I'm just going through the motions, you know? Like, I'm not really living, I'm just existing. (cries) And it's hard, because I feel like I'm supposed to be happy, like I'm supposed to be enjoying this time with my baby. But the truth is, I'm just not. I'm struggling, and I don't know how to make it stop. (pauses, taking a deep breath) Sometimes I'll have these moments where I'll feel okay, like I'll be playing with the baby, and I'll laugh, and it'll feel like the old me is back. But then it's gone, and I'm back to feeling sad and miserable. (sighs) It's just really hard to deal with, you know? Like, I feel like I'm stuck in this rut, and I don't know how to get out of it. (looks down, tears falling onto her lap) Sorry, it's just really hard to talk about...
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

(nods, tears streaming down her face) Yes, that's me. I've been crying a lot lately. It's like the smallest thing will set me off, and I'll just start sobbing. I'll be feeding the baby, or changing her diaper, and I'll just start crying because it's all just feeling so overwhelming. I've had days where I've cried for hours, just because I feel so sad and alone. (sobs) I feel like I'm losing control, like I'm just a mess all the time. And it's hard, because I don't want to be this way. I want to be strong, I want to be a good mom, I want to be happy. But it's just not happening right now. (cries) Sometimes I'll be crying, and my husband will try to comfort me, but it's hard for him to understand what I'm going through. He'll say things like "You're a great mom" or "You're doing a great job", but it's hard for me to believe that when I'm feeling so sad and overwhelmed all the time. (pauses, taking a deep breath) I just wish I could stop crying, you know? Like, I wish I could just be happy, and not feel so sad all the time. (sighs) But it's hard, because it feels like the sadness is just a part of me now. (looks down, tears falling onto her lap) Sorry, it's just really hard to talk about... (sniffles) I've been crying about once or twice a week, usually when I'm feeling really stressed or overwhelmed. It's just my way of releasing all the emotions that have been building up inside me, I guess.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

(pauses, looking down, tears welling up in her eyes) Yes... I'm so ashamed to admit it, but yes, those thoughts have occurred to me. (sniffles) It's like, in my darkest moments, when I'm feeling completely overwhelmed and hopeless, I'll have these fleeting thoughts of... of just not being here anymore. (pauses, taking a deep breath) It's not like I have a plan or anything, it's just... it's like my mind is trying to find a way to escape the pain and the sadness, and it's just a really scary thought to have. (cries) I don't want to hurt myself, I don't want to leave my baby or my husband, I just... I don't know, it's like my mind is just trying to find a way to make the pain stop. (sobs) And it's hard, because I feel like I'm supposed to be happy, I'm supposed to be this perfect mom, and I'm just not. I'm struggling, and I don't know how to make it stop. (pauses, looking up) But I want you to know that I'm not planning on harming myself, I'm not going to act on those thoughts. I just... I need help, I need someone to talk to, I need someone to help me get through this. (cries) I don't want to feel this way anymore, I want to be happy, I want to be a good mom, I want to be a good person. (sobs) Sorry, it's just really hard to talk about... (sniffles) It's just happened a few times, like once or twice in the past week, when I was feeling really overwhelmed and hopeless. But I know I need to talk about it, I need to get help, so I can be safe and be a good mom to my baby.
